setup: Stand about one arm's length from a wall, palms on it at shoulder height, feet hip-width.
steps: Brace your core so the body is one straight line.
Bend the elbows and bring your chest toward the wall.
Keep elbows about 45° from the torso.
Press the wall away until the arms are straight.
tips: Step your feet further back to make it harder before moving to the incline version.

setup: Hands on a sturdy raised surface (step, low bar or stairs), body in a straight diagonal line.
steps: Squeeze glutes and abs; keep the body straight from head to heels.
Lower the chest to the edge, elbows ~45° from body.
Press up until arms are straight.
common_mistakes: Surface that slides or is unstable
Shrugging the shoulders to the ears
tips: Lower the surface over weeks; the lower it is, the harder the push-up.

setup: Kneel, hands under shoulders, body straight from knees to head, feet lifted.
steps: Tighten abs and glutes so there is no bend at the hips.
Lower the chest to just above the floor.
Press back up with straight line knees-hips-shoulders.
common_mistakes: Sitting the hips back toward the heels
tips: Pad the knees if the floor is hard. Move to full push-ups once you hit 3 x 12.

setup: Hands slightly wider than shoulders, arms straight, body in a plank from head to heels.
steps: Squeeze glutes and abs; ribs down.
Lower the chest to a fist above the floor, elbows ~45° from the body.
Press the floor away until the elbows lock out.
tips: Think of screwing your hands into the floor to keep the shoulders stable.

setup: Plank with hands clearly wider than shoulders (about 1.5x), fingers forward or slightly out.
steps: Brace the body into a straight line.
Lower the chest between the hands with elbows out ~60-70°.
Push up to full lockout.
tips: Wider hands shift work to the chest and cut the range slightly; keep shoulder comfort first.

setup: Plank with hands together under the chest, thumbs and index fingers forming a diamond.
steps: Keep elbows tight to the sides.
Lower the chest toward the hands.
Extend fully, keeping the hips level.
tips: If the wrists complain, use narrow hands (not touching) or push-up bars.

setup: Feet on a stable raised surface (step or chair), hands on the floor under the shoulders.
steps: Stay rigid from head to heels.
Lower the chest toward the floor, elbows ~45°.
Press up without letting the hips pike.
tips: The higher the feet, the more it loads shoulders; keep it modest to start.

setup: Loop a band across your upper back and hold each end under your palms, then take a plank.
steps: Keep the body straight as the band tightens.
Lower the chest with elbows ~45°.
Press hard to lockout where the band is tightest.
common_mistakes: Letting the band slip off a hand
tips: Use a heavier band to progress without changing leverage.

setup: Wide plank, hands about twice shoulder width, fingers pointing slightly out.
steps: Shift your weight toward one hand and bend that elbow.
Keep the opposite arm straight and press it into the floor.
Lower the chest toward the bent-arm hand.
Press back to center; repeat to the other side.
tips: Use the straight arm as a kickstand and keep the movement slow.

setup: Plank with hands by the lower ribs, fingers pointing back or out, shoulders well ahead of the hands.
steps: Lean forward until the shoulders pass the hands.
Keep a hollow body: ribs down, glutes tight.
Lower under control, elbows close to the body.
Press up while holding the lean.
common_mistakes: Losing the lean as you lower
Piking the shoulders to the ears
tips: Build the wrist and bicep tolerance gradually; warm up the wrists first.

setup: Wide feet, one hand under the chest, other hand resting behind your back.
steps: Squeeze glutes, abs and legs to resist rotation.
Lower the chest toward the floor beside the working hand.
Press up while keeping shoulders and hips level.
common_mistakes: Twisting open toward the free arm
tips: Work toward it with archers or by raising the working hand on a step.

setup: Plank with straight arms, hands under shoulders.
steps: Keep elbows locked straight.
Let the chest sink slightly by squeezing the shoulder blades together.
Push the floor away to spread the blades apart and round the upper back.
tips: A small, slow movement; it teaches shoulder control for push-ups and handstands.

setup: Grip the parallel bars, jump or step to straight-arm support, legs slightly forward.
steps: Lock the elbows and push the shoulders down away from the ears.
Keep the chest slightly forward and the core braced.
Hold without swinging.
tips: Build to 30 seconds before attempting dips.

setup: Stretch a band between the bars, knees resting on it, in straight-arm support.
steps: Lower under control until the upper arms are about parallel to the floor.
Keep elbows close and chest slightly forward.
Press up to full lockout.
tips: Use thinner bands over time; slow lowering matters more than reps.

setup: Start in straight-arm support at the top of the bars.
steps: Lower slowly for 3-5 seconds, chest slightly forward.
Stop when the upper arms are parallel to the floor.
Step down or jump back to the top; repeat.
common_mistakes: Shoulders rolling forward at the bottom
tips: Stay in control; the slow lowering is the whole exercise.

setup: Support yourself on the bars with straight arms, shoulders pulled down.
steps: Lean the chest slightly forward and bend the elbows.
Lower until the upper arms are parallel with the floor.
Press back to full lockout.
common_mistakes: Going too deep with shoulders rolled forward
tips: Keep the shoulders away from the ears; stop short if the front of the shoulder hurts.

setup: From downward dog: hands shoulder-width, hips high, legs straight, head between the arms.
steps: Bend the elbows and lower the top of the head toward the floor in front of the hands.
Keep the hips high throughout.
Press back to the starting pike.
tips: Walk the feet closer to the hands to make it harder.

setup: Kick up with your belly toward the wall, hands about 20 cm from the wall, arms locked.
steps: Push tall through the shoulders, ears between the arms.
Squeeze glutes and abs to stay straight.
Breathe and hold the position.
common_mistakes: Hands too far from the wall
tips: Practice the exit (cartwheel out or step down) before long holds.

setup: Belly-to-wall handstand, hands shoulder-width, body straight.
steps: Lower the head toward the floor in a controlled path.
Lightly touch the head or a pad.
Press back up to full lockout.
tips: Use pike push-ups and short-range negatives first; place a folded mat under the head.

setup: Stand tall, kettlebell racked at the shoulder, wrist straight, feet hip-width.
steps: Squeeze glutes and abs; do not lean back.
Press straight up until the arm is fully locked, biceps by the ear.
Lower back to the rack with control.
common_mistakes: Leaning back to finish the press
tips: Pick a light bell first; the small kettlebell makes this a great shoulder finisher.

setup: Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulders, hang with arms straight and feet off the floor.
steps: Let the shoulders relax up, then gently pull them down (active hang).
Keep ribs down and legs together.
Breathe and hold.
common_mistakes: Shrugging the shoulders to the ears
tips: Great for grip and shoulder health; build to 30-60 seconds.

setup: Hang from the bar with straight arms.
steps: Keep the elbows straight.
Pull the shoulder blades down and back, lifting the body a few centimetres.
Lower slowly back to the full hang.
common_mistakes: Tiny range with no shoulder movement
tips: This teaches the first part of every pull-up.

setup: Loop a band over the bar and set one knee or foot in it; hang with straight arms.
steps: Pull the elbows down toward the ribs until the chin clears the bar.
Lower under control to straight arms.
Do not bounce out of the bottom.
tips: Use progressively lighter bands; the goal is to need less assistance.

setup: Jump or step up so your chin is over the bar, hands shoulder-width or a bit wider.
steps: Lower yourself as slowly as possible (3-5 seconds).
Keep shoulders down and body still.
Reach a full hang, then step up again.
common_mistakes: Letting shoulders shrug at the bottom
tips: Five slow reps beat ten fast drops.

setup: Underhand (palms toward you) grip, shoulder-width, hang with straight arms.
steps: Squeeze the bar and pull elbows down to the ribs.
Chin clears the bar with chest up.
Lower to straight arms under control.
common_mistakes: Craning the neck over the bar
tips: Usually easier than a pull-up because the biceps help more.

setup: Overhand grip slightly wider than shoulders, hang with straight arms, legs slightly forward.
steps: Start with the shoulder blades down.
Pull the elbows toward the ribs until the chin clears the bar.
Lower to full hang under control.
common_mistakes: Not going to full extension at the bottom
tips: If you can do 8 clean reps, make it harder with the archer or L-sit versions.

setup: Hang from parallel handles with palms facing each other (shoulder-width).
steps: Pull the elbows toward the ribs.
Bring the chin above the handles.
Lower slowly to straight arms.
tips: Often the friendliest grip on elbows and shoulders.

setup: Hang with legs straight out in front at hip height, toes pointed.
steps: Hold the legs up and pull the elbows down.
Chin clears the bar without the legs dropping.
Lower with the legs still raised.
tips: Practice a hanging L-hold first, then add the pull.

setup: Wide overhand grip, hang with straight arms.
steps: Pull toward one hand, bending that elbow.
Keep the opposite arm straight along the bar.
Lower under control; alternate sides.
tips: Build with wide-grip pull-ups and band-assisted versions first.

setup: Anchor a band at chest height (door anchor), step back until it is tight, arms straight.
steps: Brace the core and stand tall.
Pull the hands to the ribs, squeezing shoulder blades together.
Return with control.
tips: Step further back or use a thicker band to progress.

setup: Hinge forward with a flat back, knees soft, kettlebell hanging from one hand.
steps: Keep the back flat and hips back.
Row the bell toward the hip, elbow close to the body.
Lower to a straight arm without twisting.
tips: Rest the free hand on the thigh for support.

setup: Hold a band at chest height with straight arms, hands shoulder-width.
steps: Pull the band apart sideways until it touches the chest.
Squeeze the shoulder blades together.
Return slowly.
tips: Great as a warm-up or between push sets.

setup: Anchor a band at face height, hold both ends with palms facing in, step back.
steps: Pull the band toward the face, hands splitting to either side of the head.
Elbows high, finishing in a double-biceps position.
Return under control.
tips: Light band, high reps (12-20).

setup: Loop a band over the pull-up bar, hold the ends overhead with straight arms (stand or kneel).
steps: Pull the elbows down and back toward the ribs.
Squeeze the lats at the bottom.
Let the arms rise slowly.
tips: Step back so the band pulls down-forward for better line.

setup: Feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out, arms forward for balance.
steps: Brace the core and sit the hips back and down.
Keep the heels down and knees tracking over the toes.
Reach at least thigh-parallel, then drive up through the whole foot.
tips: Pause 1 second at the bottom for control.

setup: Hold the kettlebell by the horns at the chest, elbows pointing down, feet shoulder-width.
steps: Keep the bell close to the chest.
Sit between the hips, elbows inside the knees.
Drive up, chest tall.
common_mistakes: Bell drifting away from the chest
tips: The counterweight makes it easier to stay upright and go deep.

setup: Squat stance, arms ready to swing.
steps: Drop into a quarter to half squat.
Explode up, extending hips, knees and ankles.
Land softly on the midfoot and sink straight into the next rep.
tips: Land quietly; stop when you can no longer.

setup: Long staggered stance, front foot flat, back heel raised, torso upright.
steps: Lower the back knee straight down toward the floor.
Keep the front shin close to vertical.
Press through the front foot to rise.
tips: Hold a doorframe lightly for balance if needed.

setup: Stand tall, feet hip-width, hands on hips.
steps: Step one foot back and lower until both knees are about 90°.
Keep the front shin vertical and torso upright.
Push through the front heel to return.
common_mistakes: Short step, forcing the knee forward
tips: Easier on the knees than a forward lunge.

setup: Stand tall, feet together, toes forward.
steps: Step wide to the side and sit back over that leg.
Keep the other leg straight, both feet flat.
Push off the bent leg to return to standing.
common_mistakes: Heel lifting on the working leg
tips: Hold a goblet kettlebell once the bodyweight version is easy.

setup: Very wide stance, toes slightly out, arms in front for balance.
steps: Shift your weight to one side and sit deep on that leg.
Keep the other leg straight with the heel down (toes can lift).
Drive back through the bent leg to center, then switch sides.
common_mistakes: Heel of the working leg lifting
tips: Hold a doorframe at first. Great hip mobility builder.

setup: Hang a band from the pull-up bar and hold it with both hands; stand on one leg, other leg forward.
steps: Lower slowly on one leg, using the band only as needed.
Keep the free leg off the floor and the heel down.
Drive up with the working leg; reduce the pull over time.
tips: Move your hand lower on the band as you get stronger.

setup: Stand on one leg, free leg extended forward, arms forward for balance.
steps: Sit back and down on the standing leg, keeping the heel flat.
Hold the free leg straight and off the floor.
Drive up through the whole foot.
tips: Use boxes or the assisted version to build range first.

setup: Back flat on a wall, feet about 60 cm out, thighs parallel to the floor.
steps: Slide down until knees are at about 90°.
Keep the back flat on the wall and weight through the heels.
Hold and breathe.
tips: Add 10 seconds each session.

setup: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat hip-width, arms by sides.
steps: Press through the heels and lift the hips.
Squeeze the glutes at the top; body in a line from shoulders to knees.
Lower with control.
tips: Pause 2 seconds at the top.

setup: Lie on your back, one foot planted, the other leg extended.
steps: Drive through the planted heel to lift the hips.
Keep the pelvis level and the free leg in line with the thigh.
Lower slowly.
tips: Slow tempo makes it far harder.

setup: Stand tall, feet hip-width, a hand on a wall for balance if needed.
steps: Rise onto the balls of the feet as high as you can.
Pause at the top.
Lower slowly until the heels reach the floor.
common_mistakes: Rolling onto the outside of the feet
tips: Go slowly; a 3-second lowering works well.

setup: Stand on one foot, other foot lifted behind, fingertips on a wall.
steps: Rise as high as possible on the working foot.
Hold a second at the top.
Lower slowly below the floor line if standing on a step.
tips: Add reps before adding a step to extend the range.

name_fr: Soulevé de terre roumain à une jambe
setup: Stand on one foot with a soft knee, other foot just off the floor.
steps: Hinge at the hip and send the free leg straight back.
Keep a flat back and level hips until the torso is near parallel.
Squeeze the glute to stand back up.
common_mistakes: Bending the standing knee too much
tips: Touch a fingertip to a wall for balance at first.

setup: Kettlebell on the floor between the feet, feet hip-width, hips back, flat back.
steps: Grip the handle, brace, and push the floor away.
Stand tall, squeezing the glutes at the top.
Hinge back down, bell tracking close to the legs.
tips: Sets the pattern for swings.

setup: Band just above the knees, quarter-squat, feet hip-width, hands in front.
steps: Take a controlled step sideways, keeping tension on the band.
Stay low; knees pushed out over the toes.
Follow with the other foot without letting the feet touch.
tips: Take 10-15 steps each way.

setup: Forearms on the floor, elbows under shoulders, legs straight, toes down.
steps: Squeeze glutes and abs; ribs down.
Keep a straight line from head to heels.
Breathe steadily while you hold.
tips: Quality over time: stop when the hips start to sag.

setup: High plank (arms straight), feet slightly wider than hip-width.
steps: Brace the core and keep the hips level.
Lift one hand and tap the opposite shoulder.
Return it and alternate without rocking.
tips: Widen the feet to make it easier; bring them closer to make it harder.

setup: Lie on one side, forearm under the shoulder, feet stacked.
steps: Lift the hips so the body forms a straight line.
Keep the hips stacked and shoulders away from the ears.
Hold, then switch sides.
tips: Drop the lower knee to the floor to make it easier.

setup: Lie on your back, arms up toward the ceiling, hips and knees bent at 90°.
steps: Press the lower back gently into the floor.
Lower the opposite arm and leg slowly toward the floor.
Return and switch sides.
tips: Only go as low as the back stays flat.

setup: On all fours, hands under shoulders, knees under hips, back neutral.
steps: Brace the abs, then reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back.
Keep hips and shoulders level.
Pause, return, and switch sides.
tips: Imagine balancing a cup on your lower back.

setup: Lie on your back, arms overhead, legs straight.
steps: Press the lower back into the floor.
Lift the shoulders and legs off the floor, body shaped like a shallow banana.
Breathe and hold.
common_mistakes: Lower back lifting off the floor
Legs too high to be challenging
tips: Raise the legs for easier, lower them for harder; tuck knees to scale.

setup: Hang from the bar, shoulders slightly pulled down.
steps: Curl the pelvis up as the knees rise toward the chest.
Pause without swinging.
Lower slowly to a full hang.
common_mistakes: Only lifting the thighs with the hip flexors
tips: Think of curling the pelvis, not just lifting the legs.

setup: Hang from the bar, legs straight and together.
steps: Brace, and raise straight legs to hip height or above.
Keep the body still and shoulders down.
Lower with control.
tips: Start with bent knees until straight legs are controlled.

setup: Hang with a solid grip, shoulders active.
steps: Pull the bar down slightly and lift straight legs.
Touch the toes to the bar.
Lower under control without a big swing.
tips: Practice strict leg raises first.

setup: Support yourself on parallel bars, arms straight, shoulders pushed down.
steps: Lift both knees to hip height and hold them tucked.
Keep the arms locked and the chest tall.
Breathe and hold.
tips: Build time here before extending the legs.

setup: Support on the bars with arms straight, legs together.
steps: Press down hard, shoulders away from the ears.
Raise the straight legs until they are parallel to the floor.
Point the toes and hold.
tips: Even 5-10 seconds of clean holds counts; repeat short sets.

setup: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat, hands across the chest or by the temples.
steps: Curl the ribs toward the pelvis, lifting the shoulder blades.
Pause, then lower slowly.
Keep the neck relaxed.
tips: Exhale on the way up.

setup: Lie on your back, hands by the temples, legs lifted.
steps: Bring one knee toward the chest while the other leg extends.
Rotate the opposite elbow toward that knee.
Switch sides with a smooth pedaling motion.
common_mistakes: Back arching as the leg extends
tips: Slow reps work the obliques better than fast ones.

setup: Lie on your back, hands under the hips, legs straight.
steps: Press the lower back into the floor.
Raise the straight legs to vertical.
Lower slowly, stopping before the back arches.
tips: Bend the knees to regress.

setup: Lie flat, arms overhead, legs straight.
steps: Lift arms and legs at the same time.
Reach hands toward the toes, forming a V.
Lower with control, keeping the lower back flat.
tips: Bend the knees (tuck-up) if it is too hard.

setup: Sit with knees bent, lean back to about 45°, feet lifted if possible.
steps: Keep the back long and chest up.
Rotate the shoulders side to side, hands following.
Touch the floor beside each hip.
tips: Hold the kettlebell at the chest to add load.

setup: Lie face down, arms extended overhead, legs straight.
steps: Lift arms, chest and legs off the floor together.
Keep the neck neutral, looking at the floor.
Hold, then lower slowly.
tips: Pause and breathe; use short holds with repeats.

setup: Anchor a band at chest height to your side, stand sideways to it, band held at the chest.
steps: Brace and press the hands straight out in front.
Resist the band pulling you toward the anchor.
Hold a second, then bring the hands back.
tips: Step further from the anchor for more tension.

setup: On all fours, hands under shoulders, knees under hips.
steps: Inhale: drop the belly, lift the chest and tailbone (cow).
Exhale: round the back, tuck chin and tailbone (cat).
Move slowly through the whole spine.
tips: Link the movement to your breathing.

setup: Kneel, big toes together, knees apart or together, sit back on the heels.
steps: Fold forward and reach the arms in front.
Rest the forehead on the floor.
Breathe slowly into the back.
tips: Use it as a rest between hard sets.

setup: From hands and knees, tuck the toes and lift the hips up and back.
steps: Press the floor away; arms long.
Send the hips high; heels reach toward the floor.
Keep the spine long, head between the arms.
common_mistakes: Hands too close to the feet
tips: Bend the knees slightly if the hamstrings are tight.

setup: Feet shoulder-width or a little wider, toes slightly out, sink all the way down.
steps: Press the elbows against the knees, hands together.
Keep the chest tall and heels down.
Breathe and shift gently side to side.
tips: Hold a doorframe if your heels lift.

setup: Half-kneeling lunge, back knee on a pad, front foot flat ahead.
steps: Tuck the pelvis under (squeeze the back-side glute).
Shift the hips forward until you feel the front of the back hip.
Raise the same-side arm for more stretch.
common_mistakes: Knee too far past the toes
tips: Hold 30-60 seconds per side.

setup: On all fours, one hand behind the head, other hand under the shoulder.
steps: Rotate the chest toward the floor, elbow in.
Then open the chest and point the elbow to the ceiling.
Follow the elbow with your eyes.
tips: Pause at the top and exhale.

setup: Hold a band with a wide overhand grip in front of the thighs, arms straight.
steps: Lift the band overhead, arms straight.
Continue behind the head toward the lower back.
Reverse with control; widen the grip if it is too hard.
tips: Use the widest comfortable grip and go slowly.

setup: Stand tall, arms straight out to the sides at shoulder height.
steps: Draw small circles, gradually making them bigger.
Keep shoulders down and the core braced.
Switch direction halfway.
tips: Great warm-up before push or pull work.

setup: Stand tall, kettlebell held upside down by the horns at chest height.
steps: Circle the bell around the head, keeping it close.
Keep ribs down and glutes squeezed.
Alternate directions each set.
common_mistakes: Bell drifting far from the head
tips: Use a light bell: it is a mobility drill, not a strength drill.

setup: Stand tall, feet shoulder-width.
steps: Drop hands to the floor and jump or step the feet back to a plank.
Lower the chest to the floor (optional), push up.
Jump the feet in and explode up with arms overhead.
tips: Step back instead of jumping to scale; keep the pace sustainable.

setup: Stand tall, then fold forward and place the hands on the floor (knees soft if needed).
steps: Walk the hands forward to a high plank.
Pause, brace the core, keep hips level.
Walk the hands back to the feet, then stand up.
tips: Add a push-up at the plank for an extra challenge.

setup: On all fours, knees hovering a hand's width above the floor.
steps: Keep the back flat and hips low.
Move opposite hand and foot together.
Take small steps forward, then back.
tips: Crawl 5-10 meters at a time.

setup: Feet slightly wider than the shoulders, kettlebell on the floor in front; hinge and hike it between the legs.
steps: Hinge back, flat back, bell between the thighs.
Snap the hips forward to float the bell to chest height.
Let it fall and hinge back to absorb it.
common_mistakes: Lifting the bell with the arms
tips: Power comes from the hips; arms are just hooks.

setup: Stand with feet together, arms by the sides.
steps: Jump the feet apart while swinging the arms overhead.
Jump back to the start.
Land softly and stay light on the feet.
tips: Good warm-up; step-jacks are a low-impact version.

setup: High plank, hands under shoulders, body straight.
steps: Drive one knee toward the chest.
Switch legs quickly, hips level.
Keep the shoulders over the hands and the core braced.
tips: Slow it down for control; speed it up for conditioning.
